reason: Reusable complete-machine emulator covering Oric-1, Atmos, Telestrat and Pravetz 8D, with CPU, video, VIA, sound, tape/disk and debugger components.

title: ROPE — IBM 1401 programming and simulation IDE
reason: Java Swing integrated development and simulation environment for IBM 1401. Combines source editing, Autocoder invocation, SIMH process control, execution/breakpoints, memory/console/printout views and timer/UI support; original frontend source is maintained separately from bundled external engines.

title: Space Panicco — VMAP editor and PC-98 format research
reason: Historical archive by an original author augmented with concrete Space Panicco technical analysis and a working browser VMAP level editor. The editor imports/exports the original stage format, paints stage cells and validates playable actor/enemy placement. Promoted for implemented tooling and format analysis, not as recovered game source.

title: Hole in One — MSX commented disassembly
reason: Annotated recovery of HAL Laboratory's 1984 16 KB MSX golf cartridge. Includes address-anchored names/notes, executable Z80 listing and Python reconstruction of course maps, scripts and compression.

title: Kaypro — ROM, BIOS and CONFIG disassemblies
reason: Annotated recovery of multiple Kaypro II/IV boot ROMs, CP/M BIOS revisions, CONFIG utilities and character generators, with original images, assembly listings and binary-comparison scripts.

title: Neetan — Japanese computer and PC/AT emulator
reason: Rust multi-system emulator for PC-98/9821, PC-88/88VA, PC-6001, MSX, FM Towns/FM7, Sharp X68000/X1 and IBM PC/AT.

title: p50em — Prime 50-Series system emulator
reason: Jim Wilcoxson's independent C emulation of Prime 50-Series minicomputers, with disk/MAGSAV boot, R-mode save-image loading, peripheral support, tracing and PRIMOS operation.

title: smbfs / smbclient for X68000
reason: A Human68k SMB filesystem driver, mount tool and interactive client using libsmb2. It translates Human68k filesystem request packets into remote share operations, manages directory/file handles and converts Shift-JIS/UTF-8 names, making network shares available as native drives.

title: Angular PDP-1 — browser machine emulator
reason: A reusable TypeScript PDP-1 interpreter with 18-bit memory/registers, instruction groups, console switches, paper-tape loading and vector display, presented through an Angular front panel.

title: Bananaland (!Ba) recovered sources
reason: Recovered 1990–1992 SICK graphics/music demo, preserving a byte-exact RISC OS source tree and readable BBC BASIC V with inline ARM2 assembler. This is source restoration of the released v2.02 demo, recovered from PackDir SCSI-drive backups, not a new emulation wrapper.

title: RISC OS disc recovery tools
reason: Three standalone modern Python tools recover BBC BASIC V text, PackDir archives, and ADFS floppy images from Acorn RISC OS media. Implementation handles inline ARM assembler tokens, line-number references, LZW, metadata and load/execute address preservation.

title: WarCraft: Refurbished — DOS executable enhancement patches
reason: Joel Ek’s unofficial patch project for Blizzard’s WarCraft: Orcs & Humans. Actual JavaScript patch definitions contain version-specific x86 addresses and assembly bytes; the C DOS patcher checks, applies and restores binary slices.

title: ZQLoader — Spectrum audio turbo loader
reason: Host-side tape/snapshot conversion and playback tool paired with a native Z80 turbo-loader for real Spectrum 48K/128K machines. Handles TAP/TZX/snapshots, pulse generation, WAV output, compression and optional Qt UI.

title: Might and Magic III DOS — byte-exact source reconstruction
reason: C and x86 assembly reconstruction of Might and Magic III: Isles of Terra including resident code, VROOMM overlays, data and script/gameplay modules. Build tooling reconstructs and compares the original packed executable.

title: The Wall
reason: Native C64 brick-smashing puzzle/action game in C by Johan Berntsson. Reviewed main.c implements native screen/game mechanics and brick scoring; the 2020 revision added multi-brick bonuses, cursor controls and instructions, followed by a cc65-format update.

title: UNIVAC 1219 — Rust emulator, assembler and disassembler
reason: A reusable Rust implementation of the InfoAge UNIVAC 1219 machine and its programming tools. The shared crate implements 18-bit register/memory execution, instructions, arithmetic, I/O and tape handling, with CLI assembler/emulator/disassembler frontends and a browser UI. It is a substantive implementation inspired by Duane Craps’s earlier tools, rather than a packaged museum image.

title: VIEW-1108 — Apollo window-view program reconstruction
reason: A source-grounded new reconstruction of NASA MSC’s lost VIEW visualization program from its surviving reports, plots and film output. Fixed-form period-style Fortran implements trajectory, projection, spacecraft and celestial line drawing; a modern shell compiles it for live browser presentation. The project explicitly labels conjectures, modern substitutions and restomod additions rather than claiming recovered original source or an exact UNIVAC executable.

title: CodeViewParser — NB00 DOS debug-symbol reader
reason: Small Python implementation for locating early Microsoft CodeView NB00 data appended to DOS MZ executables and reading module/public-symbol subsections. Intended for symbols produced by Microsoft LINK 3.x through 5.03.

title: File Fixers
reason: Original computer-themed NES RPG made for Game Off 2021. C main controls desktop/window-style UI and game state; dungeon source creates sector layouts, tracks completion and loads entities, supported by MMC3 mapper and native assembly runtime.

title: JDasm — interactive DOS binary format analyzer
reason: Java/Swing interactive disassembler, binary format analyzer and hex editor. Includes concrete DOS COM loading/disassembly and MZ header/relocation readers alongside PE, ELF, Mach-O and media-format analyzers.

title: ZlaloX
reason: Native slalom/obstacle arcade game for the Spectrum, also ported to Amstrad CPC 464. Shared C code switches hardware/rendering and keyboard backends between the machines.

title: PM Maze — native OS/2 source continuation
reason: James L. Dean’s 1988 native maze game, carried through a 2023 GCC/ArcaOS port and a 2026 OpenWatcom restoration. It generates window-sized mazes, tracks path/backtracking and computes a visible solution.

title: Potator — Watara Supervision emulator
reason: Reusable Supervision emulator with 6502 interpreter, memory and I/O maps, interrupts, scanline GPU and sound implementations. common/gpu.c renders actual packed Supervision pixels and palette state; not a title-specific emulation wrapper.

title: Para Lander DX — C64 source
reason: Expanded 16-level parachutist landing/high-score game developed natively on C64 after a 2KB competition entry, then transferred into cross-assembly source including disk high-score support.

title: Spider Maze — C64 source
reason: Full 16-level C64 arcade maze game for Scene World issue 29 with crystals, pursuing spiders, temporary invulnerability, lives, high scores and ending sequence; distinct from abbreviated tutorial version.

title: FALLOUT.BAS — TRS-80 terminal-hacking game
reason: Native TRS-80 Model 4/4P recreation of Fallout’s terminal-hacking password puzzle, implemented in LS-DOS/TRSDOS BASIC with selectable difficulty and intelligence options. Complete readable listing plus interpreted, compiled and bootable disk forms are included.

title: GameMinder
reason: Original lightweight DOS game launcher created in 2022, with metadata filtering, play-time tracking and a PathMinder-inspired text UI. Pascal implementation launches games using a separately credited ExecWithSwap module.

title: DSP Emulator — Pascal multi-system emulator
reason: Long-running Delphi/Lazarus emulator suite with native Pascal CPU and device implementations and reusable arcade, computer and console drivers, including relatively uncommon Casio PV-1000 and Super Cassette Vision.

title: Redsea — CPC submarine shooter
reason: Original Amstrad CPC single-player shoot-em-up produced by Gameroid students for CPCRetroDev 2018. Native Z80 source includes player/enemy/bullet/control/render modules, compressed tilemaps and interrupt-driven music.

title: BUFO — Channel F road-and-river homebrew
reason: Original 2 KiB Channel F road-and-river crossing game written from scratch in Fairchild F8 assembly; includes palette tests, branch-range checks and emulator snapshot-analysis tools.

title: A940 — Elixir SDS-940 cross-assembler
reason: Elixir implementation of an SDS-940 assembler with opcode map, lexical and expression parsing, symbol resolution, pseudo-operations, relocatable address handling and assembly listing output. README is boilerplate, but substantive assembler implementation and tests establish its purpose.

title: Aqua and Ashes
reason: Native Game Boy game prototype inspired by the football section of Tiny Toons Adventures: Buster Busts Loose. Includes fixed-point object acceleration, active-object bitfields, animation, sprites, joypad and smooth parallax/background implementation.

title: NEON REVENANT — native MSX rail-shooter family
reason: Native MSX pseudo-3D rail shooter with separate MSX1, MSX2, Turbo R/V9958, V9990 and experimental V9968/Geo3D configurations. One family record prevents counting each hardware experiment as a new game.

title: AthenaOS — WonderWitch BIOS and OS reimplementation
reason: Independent native replacement for the FreyaBIOS/FreyaOS WonderWitch abstraction layer. It aims to make existing freely available WonderWitch software run with third-party WonderSwan cartridges and emulators, with BIOS services, interrupt plumbing and OS/filesystem code.

title: Big Blast
reason: Historical original MSX Asteroids-like game by Eric Boon and Manuel Bilderbeek, preserved as C source with CVS-era revision headers. Contains ship/asteroid/UFO objects, bullets, explosions, collision detection, scoring, shield-energy and level/bonus handling.

title: Pascal-Autocode — first BESM-6 Pascal compiler decompilation
reason: Recovers Pascal-Autocode version 9 (17 May 1988), descended from the first BESM-6 Pascal compiler begun in 1975. The implementation emits Cyrillic-mnemonic autocode for the BESM-6 assembler and includes editor and formatting tools.

title: iRunes
reason: A native C11 Macintosh II media player with DAAP streaming, AIFF/PCM pipeline, classic Toolbox UI and Apple Event scripting, inspired by the iTunes interface rather than recovered iTunes source.

title: Lander GBA
reason: Bare-metal ARM7TDMI port of reconstructed Archimedes Lander, using a Python source transpiler plus custom GBA display/input/RISC OS SWI replacement assembly.

title: NES Snake — native assembly game source
reason: Authored NES Snake game with a modular NESASM implementation. Game code covers persistent direction, movement ticks, pause/game-over states, snake growth and rendering, with CHR, palettes and nametables committed alongside it.

title: Rain Panic — Oric Atmos arcade game
reason: Original native arcade game in which Mr Aldo catches ceiling rain; source implements waves, character animation, hazards, score, music and fast display primitives.

title: International Karate DOS
reason: DOS assembly reconstruction with timer routines, many generic labels and explicit unresolved hard-coded-offset constraints. Modified startup means no byte-exact claim.

title: Money Idol Exchanger
reason: Banked Game Boy disassembly generated using mgbdis, with target digest and assembly scaffold. Semantic annotation completeness is not established.

title: Totoro64 — C64 cartridge fan game
reason: Studio Ghibli-inspired acorn-catching game with one/two-player modes, sprite multiplexing and IRQ-driven music. Native implementation and assets are included.

title: Amiga Depack — 68k decompressor build collection
reason: Integrated depacker source collection and build/test harness includes LZ4, RNC, Shrinkler, Cranker and other formats.

title: Maggie Library — accelerated Amiga geometry
reason: Shared/static rendering library handles texture-mapped geometry, clipping, buffers and lighting for the Maggie chipset.

title: CPCSFX — compact direct-PSG sound engine
reason: Small firmware-independent sound-effect engine drives PSG channel A from nine-byte note records with noise/envelope/vibrato flags.

title: Synergy Megademo — Turbo Assembler restoration
reason: Preserved pre-release demo source plus a substantive converter from Turbo Assembler syntax to rmac-compatible generated assembly.

title: 2048 — Amstrad PCW puzzle port
reason: Native PCW implementation of the 2048 puzzle, with board movement, score, random tiles and screen assets.

title: AFFS Tools — filesystem checking and creation
reason: AFFS structure checker and formatter, with bitmap consistency logic and verbose filesystem inspection.

title: SpaceQuest — C64 platform-engine experiment
reason: Native platform-engine experiment with map/sprite/IRQ routines and design notes. ACME entry file and module graph inspected.

title: Frogger — annotated MSX disassembly
reason: 8 KiB RC-704 cartridge, annotated control flow and game/data analysis. Primary build recipes and recursive Z80 tracing implementation inspected.

title: iffdigest — lightweight IFF and RIFF parser
reason: Small in-memory chunk-structure parser with listing and WAV examples; caller-owned buffers are referenced rather than copied.

title: Bitbendaz — palette and raster toolkit
reason: Palette remapping, gradients, raster and fade generation exports 68k data; ST/STE/Amiga quantization implementations present.

title: Visualize 1541 — G64 layout and sector inspection
reason: Circular and sector visualizations expose GCR track gaps, sync marks and missing headers/data.

title: node-iff-parser — IFF chunks and media helpers
reason: Node library exposes FORM/LIST/CAT/PROP structures plus ILBM and SMUS helpers and ByteRun unpacking.

title: C64 BASIC Langium — editor and host compiler
reason: Langium grammar, language server and generator compile BASIC-style programs to host x86-64 assembly with runtime support.

title: atrforge — extended mkatr disk toolkit
reason: Daniel Serpell mkatr/lsatr lineage with format conversion, additional validation and reorganized CLI/documentation under Atari Foundry.

title: m68kdasm — variant-aware Go disassembler
reason: Decoder exposes structured operands, symbolization and range labels with CPU-variant gating for 68000 through 68060/CPU32 and optional FPU/MMU forms.

title: Atari Tools — ATR, IMD and MAC/65 utilities
reason: ATR filesystem reader/writer and consistency repair, ATR/IMD conversion and tokenized MAC/65 source detokenization.

title: Screen Machine 3.0D — semantic Z80 reconstruction
reason: Binary-derived graphics editor restoration separates the 25,856-byte core into semantic modules with cursor/input contracts, drivers and media reconstruction.

title: DBMM — native MSX mapper-size inspection
reason: Native mapper scan reports largest detected expansion and slot through explicit bank probing and BIOS output.

title: MagSpriteEd — C64 composed sprite animation
reason: Windows editor separates sprite pools and eight-hardware-sprite frame composition, supports hires/multicolor and assembly/binary export.

title: reidrac/mkcas
reason: GitHub is only a relocation notice to git.usebox.net/mkcas. The current upstream returned a bot-check page instead of source; inspect the author-hosted implementation through an authorized accessible route before qualifying current scope.

title: CBM Font Editor — browser character-ROM editing
reason: Browser font editor maintains 256-character sets with binary/PRG, BASIC and cbmasm-style export paths.

title: iffliction — unified Amiga image and icon decoding
reason: C API detects, inspects and decodes ILBM/PBM, classic/MagicWB, NewIcons and GlowIcons into RGBA with PNG and optional SDL output.

title: ilbm — Rust image-decoder library
reason: Library reads IFF chunks and compressed/uncompressed ILBM plane rows, with info and SDL2 demonstration programs.

title: ch64edit — native C64 character-set editor
reason: Native editor provides pixel changes, shifts/rotate/mirror, clipboard, undo/redo, font loading/saving and raster-based character-set selection.

title: Snapcheck — partial Spectrum snapshot inspection
reason: Parses SZX snapshots, reports register/RAM state and loads map-file symbols as groundwork for external game assertions.

title: RetroNick2020/IFFshow
reason: Repository metadata identifies a fork of tracked mdoege/IFFshow; inspected README and Python decoder retain the same viewer/converter identity. No independent project established.

title: u64deck — Ultimate 64 control and disk tooling
reason: Self-hosted control interface integrates sector-chain D64/D71/D81 extraction, DMA loading, screen/audio streaming and device operation queues.

title: JSD Emulator Hub
reason: The README claims eighteen browser-emulator cores and several disassemblers, but per-core provenance and implementation independence remain unresolved. Inspect each core header/history and third-party lineage before deciding whether the hub or individual cores merit records.

title: amigazen/toolkit
reason: SDK distribution/collection with many shipped binaries, headers and existing component copies. No distinct source implementation selected for a new project; keep as collection discovery source. Its Codex name refers to an Amiga C lint tool, not evidence of OpenAI Codex use.

title: djh0ffman/xmtools
reason: Substantive Windows/.NET XM serialization and injector source, but README ties it to an XMPlay tracker-music demonstration; inspected source does not establish actual Amiga or C64 implementation/development relevance. Shared author alone is insufficient.

title: mstan/GumshoeNESRecomp
reason: Playable end-to-end native title port with mouse-backed Zapper support and one documented cosmetic HUD defect.

title: ocornut/meka
reason: Fresh Sega 8-bit/ColecoVision code search resolved to the already indexed MEKA emulator record; it is not a new project.

title: mstan/YoshiNESRecomp
reason: Independently runnable native title port with documented one-player, two-player and demo coverage.

title: oranguthang/flicky_src
reason: Byte-identical Mega Drive reconstruction with codecs, authoring tools and state validation.

title: depp/sparks
reason: Static gameplay/source and specific Macintosh 68k ancestry reviewed; build/run/playable/byte-exact remain unknown.

title: Arkanoid — MSX byte-exact reassembly
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: The Demon’s Forge — DOS disk-image and engine archaeology
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: SAM Coupé ROM v3.0 — corrected original source
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: Snatcher CD-ROMantic — PC Engine CD byte-exact reassembly
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: Sega 8-bit BIOS and boot-ROM disassembly collection
reason: Primary repository documentation and implementation establish multi-ROM firmware disassembly collection within tracker scope.

title: ScottTunstall/BinViewer
reason: Primary README and implementation establish a focused, directly relevant retro-binary 1bpp graphics/font exploration and extraction tool.

title: Acornsoft Lisp v4.06 — BBC Micro ROM disassembly and reassembly
reason: Primary README and implementation evidence establish the independently catalogued scope described by Acornsoft Lisp v4.06 — BBC Micro ROM disassembly and reassembly.

title: saturnkit — Sega Saturn reverse-engineering and native-port toolkit
reason: Primary README and implementation evidence establish the independently catalogued scope described by saturnkit — Sega Saturn reverse-engineering and native-port toolkit.

title: TI-99/4A cassette de/encoder
reason: WAV decoding/encoding, raw-program conversion and BASIC listing with documented cassette format and debug-wave diagnostics.

title: A09 — Motorola-family cross assembler
reason: Assembler covers several 6800/6801/6809/6301/6309/68HC11-family modes and binary, Intel HEX, S-record and FLEX relocatable outputs. RELASMB compatibility was reverse engineered and is not an exhaustive compatibility guarantee.

title: hacktools — multi-platform translation and ROM utilities
reason: Reusable extraction/repacking, graphics, text, compression and patch helpers. WonderSwan implementation splits 64 KiB banks and recalculates checksums; other platforms have individual constraints.

title: PokeLink — Neo Geo Pocket cartridge linker utility
reason: Pocket Linker parallel-port cartridge backup/write/verify source. Current master is explicitly untested by the maintainer because suitable parallel-port hardware is unavailable.

title: ToolShed — CoCo and Dragon media and development suite
reason: OS-9/DECB disk tools and historical ROM/compiler sources. Microware C material explicitly needs work; optional DiskShed GUI has a separate build. It is not uniformly complete simply because several components work.

title: Oaknut — Acorn media and metadata toolkit
reason: Unified Acorn disk/archive/BASIC toolkit with DFS/ADFS/AFS components and metadata-preserving ZIP handling. Parser resolves SparkFS, INF and filename metadata; per-filesystem operations differ.

title: ZSM4 — native relocatable Z80-family assembler
reason: Disk-based macro assembler supports Z80/Z180/Z280 instruction sets, conditional assembly and REL output suitable for L80/LINK. Source includes explicit relocatable-record generation.

title: N64Recomp — static MIPS-to-C recompilation toolkit
reason: Literal instruction-to-C translation uses function symbols, overlays and relocation metadata; delay slots and indirect calls require runtime support. Generated C is not manually recovered high-level game logic.

title: BASIC line renumberer — limited PHP implementation
reason: Implemented ASCII renumbering helper, but source contradicts universal preservation claims: it splits on colons before masking strings, and its ON branch emits literal ON ... instead of the original selector. GOTO rewriting also precedes ON-list rewriting. Not safe as an arbitrary-dialect source transformation.

title: AppleBridge — classic Mac remote development bridge
reason: Guest daemon and host protocol expose remote Apple Events, files, screenshots and native verbs over TCP or serial. Optional MCP is a frontend rather than a requirement for the bridge. ToolServer returns output, while MPW Shell fallback replies empty.

title: BlocksDS ndstool — DS ROM packaging continuation
reason: Builds/unpacks DS ROMs from components with ARM7/ARM9, overlay, banner and alignment handling. Packaging is not decompilation of game logic.

title: wAx2 — native VIC-20 assembler and monitor
reason: Integrated8KiB monitor/assembler source with BASIC-facing facilities and cartridge/PRG packaging. Real implementation despite absent root README.

title: Kweeca — native C64 music editor
reason: Editor has phrase/chain/song management, keyboard interaction and player components. Low hand travel is a design goal; fast playback and low RAM use are explicitly not current goals.

title: BBC Micro memory tester — screen-mode diagnostics
reason: Native tests exercise lower or upper16KiB under several display modes, looping until error or BREAK. Targets mode-dependent RAM symptoms, not proof of all possible hardware faults.

title: Astro Force — Master System source port
reason: Source port includes enemy/gameplay logic and banked assets, but README records stage/boss routines removed to make a build succeed. Not a confirmed complete playable game.

title: makechr — NES graphics conversion
reason: Splits pixel art into CHR/nametable/palette/attribute/sprite components; inspectedChrTile encodes two planar bitplanes. Supports diagnostics and ROM display output.

title: Ironborn65/MacCCAB
reason: Analog-board KiCad schematic reverse engineering with a stalled verification task; no software/firmware or direct software-development tool established in this tree. Outside current software tracker scope.

title: VGMComp2 — chiptune conversion and players
reason: Multi-format chiptune import, stream editing/compression and playback libraries forSN/AY/SID. InspectedCplayer documents chipselection and target wrappers; not a tracker.

title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban — GBA decompilation
reason: Matching US/Japanese reconstruction with semantic actor data and extracted graphics symbols. AI disclosure separates human-reviewed source from largely generated tools/docs.

title: Decomp Buddy — port setup and catalogue tooling
reason: Electron/CLI installation manager with published plans and optional AI repository interpretation. It orchestrates external ports; it does not itself decompile all listed games.

title: disk2easyflash — C64 disk-to-cartridge conversion
reason: Converts compatible C64 disk programs to EasyFlash cartridges using KERNAL load hooks and cartridge banking. Only LOAD-based programs are supported, not arbitrary custom loaders.

title: D71/D81 Writer — C64 physical disk transfer
reason: Native C64 utility transfers D71/D81 images from a 1541 Ultimate 2 to physical drives. Source uses KERNAL channels and block-write commands; C128 burst-mode version is only planned.

title: visrealm/vrEmuTms9918
reason: Primary documentation establishes a reusable C99 TMS9918-family VDP emulator core with a documented CMake/test path and integrations into retro systems.

title: KickAssembler binary-mirror provenance
reason: README explicitly calls this a mirror of KickAssembler binary releases, with download/check scripts rather than assembler implementation. Record dependency provenance only.

title: g0me3/fceux
reason: This is a fork of TASEmulators/fceux described only as an Oregon Trail emulator. The current repository description does not establish whether it contains a distinct debugging, analysis or preservation contribution; compare the fork diff and locate project-specific documentation before deciding whether it warrants an independent record.

title: yt-transcript-summarizer
reason: General YouTube transcript summarizer, unrelated to legacy software.

title: Detect-It-Easy
reason: General malware-oriented file detection and PE heuristics; no concrete historical-platform recovery use demonstrated for this candidate.

title: TreeFrogUI
reason: Frontend for current MIPS emulation handhelds, not an analysis or reconstruction of a historical program.

title: basf-c60.github.io
reason: Profile website repository contains only a README describing The Hobbit disassembly; the full analysis, code and generated site are in the same owner’s thehobbitv1.0 project.

title: unzx0_mips
reason: Port of Emmanuel Marty's 68000 ZX0 decompressor to PlayStation 2 MIPS R5900 and optionally PS1 R3000; the 68000 work is predecessor attribution, not the analyzed platform of this port.

title: digital-garden-workbench
reason: Python workbench for publishing the contemporary Obsidian teaching collection.

title: issues
reason: Queued tree/master/issues points into an already tracked Another World research repository; master no longer exists, while the same issues directory is present on the tracked main branch. These are the parent's research notes, not an independent project.

title: jotd666/gods-deluxe
reason: Primary Gods Deluxe README documents a substantial beta behavioral remake of the Amiga/Sega game, including observed differences and incomplete level coverage.

title: MarkyTurtle/TTEDiskBuilder-netcore
reason: README identifies a .NET Core port of h0ffman’s existing ADF disk builder for VS Code; a useful development utility, but no separate reconstructed historical format or subject analysis is demonstrated.

title: Atari ST/STE/Falcon game ports
reason: Collection porting the author's Amiga games using Atari graphics/audio/OS compatibility layers. Requirements vary by game from ST through Falcon CT60; not all games target baseline ST.

title: War in Middle Earth MSX disassembly
reason: Annotated MSX cassette disassembly covering Spectrum-derived loader and relocated game blocks. ZX lineage is documented without classifying this as a separate Spectrum restoration.

title: Lost Vikings 3 Project Engine
reason: SDL/CMake engine and editor for a Lost Vikings fan project. README identifies missing supplementary files and old build dependencies; a complete playable release is not established.

title: Sonic Blast Game Gear disassembly
reason: Early WLA-DX disassembly for US/EU Sonic Blast; ROM-splitting and build scripts exist. Japanese G Sonic support remains prospective.

title: Jetpac cartridge fork
reason: README identifies mrcook original project already tracked.

title: Generic Tile Engine — Apple IIgs
reason: Native IIgs super-hires tile engine with two scrolling layers and software sprites. Source, macros and demos present; performance/runtime not independently measured.

title: ZX Spectrum isometric engine experiments
reason: Filmation-style routines, masked sprites, object behavior and physics tests. Explicitly engine experimentation rather than a complete game.

title: LineWars II — SDL3 port of reconstructed DOS engine
reason: Distinct SDL3 backend port of the already tracked DOS C reconstruction. Sample entry point documents built-in mission/model fallback when GAME.DAT is absent. Port and verification claims are upstream claims; do not imply independently proven full-game coverage.

title: Star Raiders — Python educational reconstruction
reason: Tutorial-oriented Python reconstruction with source-line references to the original Atari code. Inspected AI contains original velocity-table references but uses Python mechanisms; fidelity is attributed, not verified. Repository description mentions TypeScript, but inspected main tree establishes Python only.

title: go6502 — CPU and development-tool suite
reason: General CPU emulator, assembler, disassembler and debugger packages with source-map-aware console host. No machine peripherals implied; not a game-specific emulator.

title: Color Computer ROM-to-RAM routine analysis
reason: Short commented position-independent routine recovered from embedded BASIC machine-code DATA, explaining ROM/RAM mapping and interrupt handling. Narrow utility, not complete system ROM.

title: New Super Mario Bros. — DS decompilation
reason: Early matching project with actor/base sources. README explicitly says it cannot compile to a full ROM yet; do not imply a playable reconstruction.

title: TCH board emulation and disassembly research
reason: Substantive board-family analysis and MAME driver repairs, but its primary delivered restoration is emulation. Retain in audit backlog rather than promoting as a native source port; separately review the reusable disassembly output.

title: Hunkster — Amiga data-object generator
reason: Windows utility writing HUNK data/external-symbol records for vbcc/Free Pascal linking. Narrow Amiga-oriented predecessor to the separately reviewed multi-format rtbinobj.

title: Swabby — Game Gear source
reason: Author-recovered homebrew game source with level setup, VRAM initialization, assets and PSG library. No independent build/playability test.

title: Console Graphics Converter
reason: PNG-to-console tile data with palette constraints, tile deduplication and binary/ASM/C exports. Palette quantization is imperfect; embedded palettes recommended. Inspected SNES tile/palette implementation.

title: Minakuchi Game Boy disassembly collection
reason: Mega Man I/III/IV/V and Bionic Commando share related code lineage. Keep root collection whole; original ROM slices fill gaps. Mega Man II deliberately excluded because its developer/codebase differs.

title: Vib-Ribbon PAL decompilation
reason: Partial C reconstruction of originally C++ game modules. Sample mixes actual C, NON_MATCHING alternatives and INCLUDE_ASM; upstream does not guarantee behavioural equivalence of non-matching paths. Own executables required.

title: GEMS Mega Drive research toolkit
reason: Sequence splitting/combining, instrument conversion and MIDI export source for GEMS sound data. Root toolkit is distinct from original sound driver and signature-only datasets; no equivalence tests run.

title: Helix Apple II bubble-memory firmware
reason: Partially reversed firmware3.40 with named ProDOS/bubble-controller state and Macro Assembler AS build route. Source evidence exists despite no README; completeness and exact matching unverified.

title: Ophis 65xx cross-assembler
reason: Lexer/parser and assembler for 6502,65C02,4502/4510 and undocumented6510 opcodes. Host portability and supported variants are upstream claims, not independent build results.

title: follow9 6x09 disassembler
reason: Browser control-flow-following disassembler derived from dasm09. Source and tests present; code/data separation is a technique, not a guarantee every indirect target is recovered.

title: GBA library-function signatures
reason: Text patterns plus FLIRT/YARA/radare signatures for dated library revisions. Sample identifies BIOS-call wrappers. Signature matches are version-bound heuristics, not full source reconstruction.

title: Reginald and the She Vampires — native CPC remake and sequel
reason: Native C remake/reboot and sequel of the named 1987 game. The substantial game modules implement movement, monsters, menus, sarcophagi, levels, victory and defeat. title: ZVM Sega — partial Z-machine interpreter for SD-1000-expanded SC-3000
reason: Reusable Infocom Z-machine v3 interpreter, with opcode/operand decoding, text/dictionary/object/stack modules and story banks. This is a language virtual machine, not emulation of an original physical game CPU and not a game-specific CPU-emulation execution path. Partial game-agnostic Z-machine v3 runtime requiring SD-1000-style 16 KiB unmirrored RAM; stock Sega memory layouts are unsupported. Does not run correctly on stock SG-1000/SC-3000 or standard Master System RAM layouts. README-equivalent hardware document contains both updated local patched-emulator claims and older unverified statements; no verified supported runtime here. Memory output stream is unimplemented, window handling is minimal, save/restore are stubs. Keep partial status and label SC-3000 with SD-1000 caveat. No top-level project license detected. SGlib has its own license; bundled Mini-Zork story and generated bank source do not establish permission for arbitrary redistribution.

title: BGUI — preserved Amiga BOOPSI GUI framework
reason: baseclass.c implements BOOPSI object creation/render/layout/interaction and retains long historical RCS change notes; bgui_init.c opens native Amiga library dependencies. SAS/C build has standard/debug/enhanced variants; enhanced explicitly selects CPU=68020, while historical build notes say the standard build supports OS 2/68000. Historical standard-build compatibility is a documented claim, not a tested current deployment profile. AROS support is visible in conditional source/build layout, but no new AROS platform label or tested AROS runtime is claimed. LICENSE.md is BSD-3-Clause, while LICENSE has an older use/copy permission notice; retain both and per-file copyrights rather than asserting uniform relicensing.

title: iffparse and iffar — Amiga IFF inspection and archive tools
reason: main.c parses/displays IFF chunk metadata through Amiga iffparse.library and supports file/clipboard modes. iff.c and companion archive sources preserve an iffar lineage based on Karl Lehenbauer’s public-domain 1988 EA IFF code, ported to Amiga DOS I/O/C89. SMakefile builds iffparse and iffar as one related command suite. The repository name must not be mistaken for a recreation of Commodore’s iffparse.library. BUILD.md calls the default CPU 68020, but inspected SCOPTIONS/SMakefile do not enforce an explicit CPU flag; retain this as documented intent. SAS/C 6.58 and NDK 3.2R4 are required; no independent parsing/round-trip corpus validation.

title: NetBSD rump — incomplete AmigaOS 4 network-stack port
reason: Substantive work-in-progress port provides PowerPC/AmigaOS adaptation for NetBSD rump kernel threads, memory, locks, timers and IPC, plus a socket-library shim architecture. Inspected osal_thread.c implements native Exec task creation/join and rump hypercall wrappers; fdtable.c deliberately provides an in-memory socket scaffold. Latest NEXT_STEPS.md supersedes stale README status: rump_init has been run, reaches about 15 adaptation-layer calls, then reproducibly faults in an OS4 library. Not a functioning TCP/IP stack. Real network dispatch, full BSD API and driver bridge are incomplete; documented deterministic DSI crash blocks initialization. Makefile/build reports prove only upstream partial compilation/symbol closure, not working networking. No local compilation or execution. NetBSD-10 source is imported separately and retains its own licenses; no root license was found for project-specific glue.
